issues.quote: On the multifamily side, the same Terner Center study reported that in California, lenders on small projects often require completion guarantees
issues.problem: TERNER24 (C33) talks about small missing-middle projects, which can include 2-4-unit buildings. It does not say this is multifamily (5+) lending. The label 'multifamily side' puts the source's finding in a category it doesn't name.
issues.fix: For small projects, the same Terner Center study reported that in California, lenders often require completion guarantees and "recourse to the developer's personal assets."

issues.quote: The International Building Code is a model code; Seattle's code, for example, reprints its text.
issues.problem: Seattle reprints the IBC text with local amendments. The six-story single-stair rule (C18) is one of those amendments. As written, the line says Seattle copies the IBC, and two sentences later says Seattle's code allows something the IBC forbids.
issues.fix: The International Building Code is a model code; Seattle's code, for example, reprints its text, with local amendments.

issues.quote: In the model code's 2021 edition — the version we checked —
issues.problem: The channel read the IBC table through Seattle's official reprint (the ICC site returned a reCAPTCHA). The script says it checked the model code directly.
issues.fix: In the model code's 2021 edition — as reprinted in Seattle's 2021 code, which we checked —

issues.quote: a group that advocates single-stair rules
issues.problem: Imprecise: CBNA advocates loosening the single-stair limits. 'Advocates single-stair rules' could also read as backing the current rules.
issues.fix: a group that advocates allowing more single-stair buildings

issues.quote: In the Department of City Planning's final plan for that vote, these "missing middle" buildings had been "functionally banned by zoning."
issues.problem: The Final Plan describes changes already adopted, so 'for that vote' is not supported. In the source, 'functionally banned by zoning' refers to the existing buildings that the new ones will match.
issues.fix: In the Department of City Planning's final plan, the new "missing middle" buildings match the scale of existing buildings that had been "functionally banned by zoning."

issues.quote: Then we'll look at the forces outside the rules: costs, interest rates and rents.
issues.problem: C58 says 'borrowing costs', not interest rates. 'Rates' in segs 07 and 11 has the same gap.
issues.fix: Then we'll look at the forces outside the rules: building and borrowing costs, and rents. (In 07 and 11, change "costs, rates and rents" to "costs, borrowing costs and rents".)

issues.quote: or the traffic and local-character concerns raised there

issues.quote: A 2023 study by Urban Institute researchers linked loosening land-use reforms
issues.problem: Only the abstract was read. nguon/E-cai-cach.md notes a methods critique (AEI Housing Center, 27/10/2025) that the script leaves out, even though the study is used as evidence of increases.
issues.fix: Add after the sentence: "The AEI Housing Center has questioned the study's methods." (add claim with AEI source), or keep as is and note in claims.md why the critique is left out. Read beyond the abstract if possible.

issues.quote: When Washington state's legislature heard its 2023 middle-housing bill, supporters called it
issues.problem: The only documented place this expectation or concern appears is one committee hearing (C61). claims.md does not show it is widely heard. The on-screen COMMON CLAIM ↔ RECORD frame is not specified.
issues.fix: No script change. In claims.md §4, add other public places the claim appears (e.g., the STERLING agenda item C38, the Terner 2021 SB 9 estimate C37). Specify the COMMON CLAIM ↔ RECORD visual with the source on the RECORD side.

issues.quote: which, as of October 12th, has not been published.
issues.problem: The as-of marker on an ongoing matter has no year.
issues.fix: which, as of October 12, 2026, has not been published.

issues.fix: Keep the narration. On screen, label each figure with its series (NRC or CNH) and its start year, and add the CNH note on sampling error for small buildings in 2025.
